summary: Re-tested M5-S05 (build-level package.xml + deploy-order note) after its documented -> running -> built rebuild added the TestUserFactory ApexClass member. All 3 declared acceptance tests plus both always-on checks (xml, manifest) passed; check-outputs is ok. The manifest check was run whole-tree across artefacts/ (119 files, 57 deployable, 57 members, 0 missing either direction) rather than scoped to M5-S05's own directory, per the reading standards/build-orchestration.md establishes for a build-level manifest step and the same reading the step's earlier test run applied. Step moved built -> tested.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran or was correctly classified as manual, both always-on checks completed over the full re-derived file set, and every result (checker exit 0, xml 1/1 parse, manifest 0 missing either direction, check-outputs ok) came from an exit code or JSON payload this run observed directly. No checker was refused, no manifest coverage-gap exclusion was needed, and no declared checker was missing.

process_observations.observation: The build-level manifest rebuild was fully self-consistent: the only member diff across all 119 artefact files was the single +TestUserFactory ApexClass member the deploy-order.md § 0 rebuild record predicted, and the whole-tree two-way check found zero missing members in either direction.

M3-S05 and M5-S02, both blocked, own no directory at all under artefacts/, so they contribute zero files and zero members to the whole-tree check by construction rather than by a special-cased exclusion rule the checker has to remember.

The declared checker command (check_deployment_manifest.py) exits 0 on this manifest only because SharingRules findings were downgraded from HIGH to WARN in a prior rebuild (fa3cad053); a reviewer relying on exit code alone would not see that a sharing rule is shipping without that being a hard gate.

agents/step-tester/AGENT.md Step 3 states the manifest rule as 'for every artefact file [under the step's artefact directory]', with no explicit carve-out for a build-level docs step whose own directory holds no component files; this run followed the same whole-tree reading the step's prior test run applied (justified by deploy-order.md § 5.1's own explicit 'whole artefacts/ tree' language), but the playbook itself does not yet state the exception.
Now that M5-S05 is tested, the three W12 manual tests and the checker's SharingRules WARN are ready for the M5 milestone gate read.
process_observations.followup_reason: because M5 is the build's final milestone and milestone-verifier owns the cross-step and milestone-scoped acceptance read this step's manual tests defer to.

process_observations.observation: M5-S05 is now tested but not yet re-documented after this rebuild; build-doc-keeper last ran on the pre-rebuild (56-member) state.
